reuseNote: All exemplars new in this run. Web search budget ran out after 15 searches; some sources (Pomodoro, Getting Things Done, adult ADHD screener) could not be opened and are unverified. Repair run copied from 20261019-140017.

self-forgiveness-exams.name: Self-forgiveness and procrastination study (Wohl, Pychyl and Bennett)
self-forgiveness-exams.outcome: 134 first-year students who forgave themselves for procrastinating before first exams procrastinated less before the second
self-forgiveness-exams.limits: One student sample; correlational survey, nobody was assigned to forgive themselves.
self-forgiveness-exams.locator: "it did predict better performance in the second set"

mood-repair.name: Procrastination as short-term mood repair (F. Sirois and T. Pychyl)
mood-repair.outcome: Review argues procrastination is mainly about escaping bad feelings now, at the cost of the future self
mood-repair.limits: A theory review, not a trial; it explains rather than tests a fix.
mood-repair.locator: "has a great deal to do with short-term mood repair and emotion regulation"

if-then-plans.name: Implementation intentions meta-analysis (Gollwitzer and Sheeran), as cited in a 2021 review
if-then-plans.outcome: Specific when-where plans improved goal attainment, d = 0.65
if-then-plans.limits: Opened a 2021 Frontiers meta-analysis that cites the 2006 review, not the chapter itself; that 2021 review found a smaller effect and signs of publication bias.
if-then-plans.locator: "implementation intentions had a positive effect on improving goal attainment"

coin-flip-decisions.name: Heads or Tails coin-toss experiment (Steven Levitt)
coin-flip-decisions.outcome: People told by a coin to make a change they were stuck on were happier six months later
coin-flip-decisions.limits: Volunteers who chose to take part; self-reported happiness; the author notes large effects may be overestimates.
coin-flip-decisions.locator: "substantially happier two months and six months later"

focusmate.name: Focusmate virtual body doubling
focusmate.outcome: Paired 25-, 50- or 75-minute video work sessions; three free sessions a week
focusmate.limits: A paid service beyond the free tier; no outcome study opened.

stickk.name: stickK commitment contracts
stickk.outcome: Co-founder reported 78% of users with money and a referee reached goals, versus 35% with no money down
stickk.limits: Success figures come from the company's co-founder and are not independently checked; people who choose to bet differ from those who don't.
stickk.locator: Founded 2007 by Yale professors Dean Karlan and Ian Ayres

freedom-blocker.name: Freedom website and app blocker
freedom-blocker.outcome: Blocks chosen sites and apps across devices; $39.99 a year, limited free version
freedom-blocker.limits: Company's own page; user counts on the page disagree (4M+ vs 3.5M); no outcome study.
freedom-blocker.locator: "Freedom is the only app that can sync blocking sessions across all your devices"

shut-up-write.name: Shut Up & Write sessions
shut-up-write.outcome: Free in-person and online sessions: say your goal, work quietly together, check in at the end
shut-up-write.limits: Built for writers, though the format works for other tasks; no outcome data.
shut-up-write.locator: "Every session, in person and online, is free."

chadd-directory.name: CHADD professional directory
chadd-directory.outcome: Searchable directory of ADHD clinicians, coaches and clinics (717 results at access)
chadd-directory.limits: Listings are not an endorsement; check credentials and insurance yourself.

nimh-adhd.name: National Institute of Mental Health overview of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
nimh-adhd.outcome: ADHD symptoms begin in childhood and usually continue into the teen years and adulthood
nimh-adhd.limits: General overview; no adult-specific diagnosis guidance on the page.
nimh-adhd.locator: "Symptoms begin in childhood and usually continue into the teen years and adulthood."

jan-adhd.name: Job Accommodation Network ADHD accommodations
jan-adhd.outcome: Free, confidential advice; ADHD list includes to-do lists, priority-setting help, a mentor, timers and calendar apps
jan-adhd.limits: Advice service, not an enforcer; what an employer must grant depends on the Americans with Disabilities Act and the facts of the job.

auto-enroll-401k.name: Automatic 401(k) enrollment study (Brigitte C. Madrian and Dennis F. Shea)
auto-enroll-401k.outcome: 401(k) participation significantly higher when new hires were enrolled unless they opted out; the default contribution rate and investment allocation strongly influenced what participants saved
auto-enroll-401k.limits: One company; many workers stayed at a low default contribution rate.
auto-enroll-401k.locator: NBER Working Paper 7682, issued May 2000: "401(k) participation is significantly higher under automatic enrollment."

nyc-court-texts.name: New York City summons redesign and text reminders
nyc-court-texts.outcome: Texts with consequences and a planning prompt cut missed court dates 26%; 36% with redesigned form
nyc-court-texts.limits: Low-level summonses only; figures from the university's news release.
nyc-court-texts.locator: "the total decline in the rates of failure-to-appear in court was 36 percent"

sweden-prefilled-tax.name: Sweden's pre-filled tax return
sweden-prefilled-tax.outcome: Tax agency pre-enters income reported by employers and banks; approve by e-service, text or phone if nothing changes
sweden-prefilled-tax.limits: Relies on national ID and employer reporting; people with business income still have to add details.
sweden-prefilled-tax.locator: "via our e-service, or by text message or phone call"

irs-direct-file.name: IRS Direct File pilot
irs-direct-file.outcome: 140,803 people filed free directly with the IRS; 90% of surveyed users rated it excellent or above average
irs-direct-file.limits: Pilot in 12 states with simple returns only; politically contested; status after 2024 not checked in this run.
irs-direct-file.locator: "We saw a strong response from the pilot."

pomodoro.name: Pomodoro Technique (Francesco Cirillo)
pomodoro.outcome: Developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s, when he was a university student, using a tomato-shaped kitchen timer; work intervals typically 25 minutes with short breaks
pomodoro.limits: Opened the Wikipedia article, not Cirillo’s own pages (404 in this run); describes the method, not an outcome study.

gtd-next-action.name: Getting Things Done next actions (David Allen)
gtd-next-action.outcome: David Allen’s method: for each actionable item, decide the next action, and the project if more than one action is needed
gtd-next-action.limits: The official method page; describes the method, not an outcome study. Year not shown on the page opened.

asrs-screener.name: Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale six-question screener (World Health Organization workgroup)
asrs-screener.outcome: Developed in conjunction with the World Health Organization and the Workgroup on Adult ADHD; the screener is six questions (Part A)
asrs-screener.limits: Opened the Wikipedia article; the Harvard-hosted PDF returned 503. The page does not say whether the scale is free. A screener is not a diagnosis.
asrs-screener.locator: "in conjunction with the World Health Organization"

focusmate-body-doubling.name: Focusmate article on body doubling
focusmate-body-doubling.outcome: Body doubling means working with another person present, in person or virtually, while they do something unrelated; term coined by ADHD coach Linda Anderson in 1996; reported benefits strongest among people with ADHD but not limited to them
focusmate-body-doubling.limits: Written by Focusmate, which sells body-doubling sessions; describes the practice rather than testing it.
focusmate-body-doubling.locator: "Their only job is to be there."
